thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: dedicated-resv-pool-usw2-4 GPU utilization 100% (20/20), queue_depth=1208, autoscaler_attempts=6, last_error=ScaleToMaxReached. severity=high :rotating_light:

alex: paging on-call (I'm up). seeing the bot — queue is wild. tagging infra.

marta: looking at dashboards now. 95th latency for reserved tenants spiked to 3.8s -> request throttles increasing.

suresh: quick summary from autoscaler logs: attempted scale 20 -> 25, provider rejected: "quotaExceeded: maximum-eni-per-subnet" reported. autoscaler stuck at max_nodes=20.

jamal: confirmed. reservation pool is pinned at max. we have several long-running sessions from OrchidBank eating persistent GPU slots (approx 15 of 20 GPUs). suspect noisy-tenant.

marta: OrchidBank is a reserved enterprise tenant on this pool (resv_id=rsv-143). their job mix includes very long sequence evals + KV-cache heavy sessions.

alex: immediate goal: reduce queue and prevent customer impact for other enterprise tenants (BrightLeaf, NovaHealth). suggestions?

suresh: options:
- enable per-tenant rate limiting on OrchidBank
- trigger eviction policy for best-effort and preemptible jobs
- request emergency quota bump from cloud (slow)
- route some enterprise traffic to fallback region if allowed (eu-west may have capacity)

jamal: we can apply per-tenant throttling via our control plane: run
```
redwoodctl tenants update --tenant orchidbank --max_concurrency 2 --burst 0
```
This will preserve their reservation but cap concurrent new sessions.

ops-bot: ACTION ADDED: apply-tenant-throttle (assigned to suresh) — due at +5m.

suresh: running the throttle command now. tailing scheduler logs.

suresh: COMMAND OUTPUT:
```
> redwoodctl tenants update --tenant orchidbank --max_concurrency 2 --burst 0
ok: tenant orchidbank updated
```

marta: seeing a small drop in queue of best-effort jobs. reserved tenants still have some waiting requests for short bursts.

alex: support, please notify customers likely to be impacted proactively. @support-elena can you take?

support-elena: opening support thread and incident SMS to OrchidBank and BrightLeaf. message: "We are actively mitigating a capacity event in us-west-2 affecting reserved sessions; you may see degraded throughput for short periods. On-call is applying temporary throttles and eviction policies."

jamal: scheduler logs show active preemption of preemptible pods. snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T03:11:05Z] scheduler: preempting job id=pr-98765 reason=noisy-tenant, freed_gpus=2
[2026-03-15T03:11:06Z] scheduler: evicted best-effort job id=be-3344
```

marta: also seeing increased thundering herd on checkpoint writes from OrchidBank sessions — KV-cache pressure. might need to limit max_sequence_length for them as a next step.

alex: can we spin up an emergency reserved pool in another AZ/region and shift some tenants? what is the fastest safe route?

suresh: fastest is to route non-latency-sensitive reserved tenants to eu-west-1 if their config allows cross-region. spinning a new reserved pool requires procurement approval for dedicated capacity, but we can temporarily failover individual tenants to hosted fallback models (lower memory/quantized) immediately.

jamal: action: provision fallback model routes for NovaHealth and BrightLeaf to reduce pressure on reserved pool. I can flip routing for those two in 8-10m.

ops-bot: ACTION ADDED: failover-brightleaf-novahealth (assigned jamal) — due +15m.

marta: also adding a short-term rule to preferentially evict long-running interactive sessions that are idle. policy snippet:
```
policy evict_idle_sessions {
  idle_threshold = 300s
  target = best_effort, interactive_long
}
```
Applied.

alex: update on customer-visible metrics?

marta: queue_depth now 48 (was 1208). GPU util down to 82% across pool (some warmdown). throttles for OrchidBank up, but their new session success rate is steady at ~88%.

support-elena: OrchidBank replied: "we see degraded throughput but your throttling helped. please keep us posted."

alex: good. next: we need a follow-up plan — short/medium/long term items. I'll list and we can assign.
Short-term (<=24h):
- keep per-tenant throttle on OrchidBank until quota bump or behavioral mitigation (owner: suresh)
- failover NovaHealth/BrightLeaf to fallback routes (owner: jamal)
- support notifications & post-incident customer comms (owner: support-elena)

Medium-term (1-2 weeks):
- request/enforce cloud quotas increase or change subnet strategy to avoid ENI/IP exhaustion (owner: infra)
- implement noisy-tenant detection alert with automatic soft-throttle (owner: eng-runtime)
- review eviction thresholds and KV-cache limits (owner: eng-ml)

Long-term: consider autoscaler changes to respect per-reservation headroom and predictive scaling by sequence length distribution.

marta: opening an incident ticket in JIRA: RED-INC-2026-0315. added logs and action items.

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity -> high -> mitigated. queue cleared to normal thresholds.

alex: thanks all. I'll hand this to postmortem owners. tagging @suresh @jamal @support-elena for follow-ups. :thumbsup:

suresh: leaving the throttle in place for 6h, monitoring. if we get quota bump, we'll roll back.

jamal: failover complete for NovaHealth and BrightLeaf — both traffic now to hosted-fallback-quantized models. latency up ~120ms but within SLA for those tenants.

support-elena: customers updated, internal status page updated.

alex: closing thread for active paging. postmortem owner: marta. timeline created.

ops-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED: mitigation stable. final queue_depth=12, GPU_util=48%.

marta: postmortem note: root cause = combination of (1) high sustained job mix from reserved tenant OrchidBank, (2) autoscaler hit cloud provider limits (ENI/IP quota) causing scale-to-max, (3) lack of automatic noisy-tenant soft-throttle. recommendations captured in RED-INC-2026-0315.

alex: good work everyone. we'll use this in our quarterly reliability review. :clap:"
